The `inputs` are a list of file sets, runtime inputs, and environment variables that affect the output of the target.
If any of the `inputs` change, the cache is invalidated and the target is re-run.

In CI with [`NX_IO_SNAPSHOTS`](/docs/reference/environment-variables) set, Nx can hash a task from the files it read on a recorded run instead of its declared file sets, so a change to a declared file that run didn't read doesn't re-run it.
-Set [`sandbox.backfill: false`](/docs/reference/project-configuration#sandbox) on a target to keep its declared inputs authoritative.
+Set [`ultracache.mode: "warn"`](/docs/reference/project-configuration#ultracache) on a target to keep its declared inputs authoritative.

Nx errs on the side of caution when using inputs. Ideally, the "perfect" configuration of inputs will allow Nx to never re-run something when it does not need to. In practice though, it is better to play it safe and include more than strictly necessary in the inputs of a task. Forgetting to consider something during computation hash calculation may lead to negative consequences for end users. Start safe and fine-tune your inputs when there are clear opportunities to improve the cache hit rate.

The first path segment cannot contain `*`, so `**/generated/**` is not supported. `?`, `!`, `[`, `]` and extglobs are not supported either. Nothing reports these at authoring time, so the pattern has no effect. Anchor it to a directory instead, such as `libs/*/generated/**`.

-Set `"backfill": false` to keep tracking the target but hash it from its declared inputs and outputs. By default, a recorded snapshot backfills both: the reads it observed replace the target's declared filesets, and the writes it observed extend its outputs. A target whose inputs depend on dynamic behavior or external state can't be described that way, so it should opt out.
-Reads and writes are one switch. A task hashed from its recorded reads but cached from its declared outputs would describe a run that never happened.
+Reads and writes move together. A task hashed from its recorded reads but cached from its declared outputs would describe a run that never happened, so no mode applies one without the other.

-`backfill` only applies where Nx hashes from a recorded snapshot. That's in CI with [`NX_IO_SNAPSHOTS`](/docs/reference/environment-variables) or `NX_CLOUD_USE_IO_SNAPSHOTS` set, and only for tasks a snapshot was recorded for. Everywhere else, a task hashes from its declared inputs and caches its declared outputs.

+Nothing outside Nx Cloud records or applies IO, so every mode behaves as `off` without it. Applying a recording additionally needs [`NX_IO_SNAPSHOTS`](/docs/reference/environment-variables) or `NX_CLOUD_USE_IO_SNAPSHOTS` set in CI, and a recording for the task in question.
